title: Prakrama 4, Sarga 10. Beholding the Sacred Bowers, the Yamuna and Other Places
html:
Krishnadasa goes on showing the Lord the places of Vraja: where Rama and Krishna in spring attire danced with the gopis and slew Shankhachuda; Kumudavana; the Ambika forest, where Sudarshana was delivered; the town of Vrishabhanu, where Radha appeared; Raivataka Hill, where Baladeva crushed Dvivida and drew the Yamuna to Himself; Pavana Lake; Kamyavana with Picchala Hill; Khadiravana and the bowers of Radha and Madhava; hearing of them, the Lord weeps and once more reveals to the world the mood of the cowherd village

Verse 1

ततश्च पश्यात्र वसन्तवेशौ श्रीरामकृष्णौ व्रजसुन्दरीभिः।
चिक्रीडतुः स्वस्वयूथेश्वरीभिः समं रसज्ञौ कलधौतमण्डितौ॥१॥

tataśca paśyātra vasantaveśau śrīrāmakṛṣṇau vrajasundarībhiḥ|
cikrīḍatuḥ svasvayūtheśvarībhiḥ samaṁ rasajñau kaladhautamaṇḍitau||1||

tatah — then; cha — and; pashya — behold; atra — here; vasanta-veshau — in spring attire; shri-rama-krishnau — Sri Rama and Krishna; vraja-sundaribhih — with the beauties of Vraja; chikridatuh — sported; sva-sva-yutha-ishvaribhih — with the leaders of their respective groups; samam — together; rasa-jnau — the two knowers of rasa; kaladhauta-manditau — adorned with gold.

1"And now behold this place: here Sri Rama and Krishna, the knowers of rasa, in spring attire and adorned with gold, sported with the beauties of Vraja — with the leaders of Their groups.

Verse 2

नृत्यन्तौ गोपीभिः सार्धं गायन्तौ रभसान्वितौ।
गायन्तीभिश्च रामाभिर्नृत्यन्तीभिश्च शोभितौ॥२॥

nṛtyantau gopībhiḥ sārdhaṁ gāyantau rabhasānvitau|
gāyantībhiśca rāmābhirnṛtyantībhiśca śobhitau||2||

nrityantau — dancing; gopibhih — with the gopis; sardham — together; gayantau — singing; rabhasa-anvitau — full of ardour; gayantibhih — singing; cha — and; ramabhih — by the lovely women; nrityantibhih — dancing; cha — and; shobhitau — graced.

2They danced with the gopis and sang, full of ardour, and the lovely women, singing and dancing, were Their adornment.

Verse 3

तयोरित्थं विहरतोः शङ्खचूडश्च दुर्मतिः।
कदर्थयन् गोपीजनान् ताभ्यां समुपलक्षितः॥३॥

tayoritthaṁ viharatoḥ śaṅkhacūḍaśca durmatiḥ|
kadarthayan gopījanān tābhyāṁ samupalakṣitaḥ||3||

tayoh — while the two; ittham — thus; viharatoh — were sporting; shankhachudah — Shankhachuda; cha — and; durmatih — the wicked; kadarthayan — molesting; gopi-janan — the gopis; tabhyam — by the two; samupalakshitah — was noticed.

3While They sported thus, the wicked Shankhachuda began to molest the gopis, and the two brothers caught sight of him.

Verse 4

हृतमस्य शिरोरत्नं कृष्णेनापि हतः खलः।
दत्तं श्रीबलदेवाय मणिरत्नं स्यमन्तकम्॥४॥

hṛtamasya śiroratnaṁ kṛṣṇenāpi hataḥ khalaḥ|
dattaṁ śrībaladevāya maṇiratnaṁ syamantakam||4||

hritam — was taken; asya — his; shiro-ratnam — crest-jewel; krishnena — by Krishna; api — and; hatah — slain; khalah — the villain; dattam — given; shri-baladevaya — to Sri Baladeva; mani-ratnam — the jewel; syamantakam — Syamantaka.

4Krishna slew the villain and took the jewel from his head; and that precious stone, the Syamantaka1, was given to Sri Baladeva.

Verse 5

पश्यन्तीनां च गोपीनां श्रीकृष्णेन सकौतुकम्।
तेनापि तन्निजप्रेष्ठैर्दत्तं तत्प्रेयसीं प्रति॥५॥

paśyantīnāṁ ca gopīnāṁ śrīkṛṣṇena sakautukam|
tenāpi tannijapreṣṭhairdattaṁ tatpreyasīṁ prati||5||

pashyantinam — as (they) looked on; cha — and; gopinam — the gopis; shri-krishnena — by Sri Krishna; sa-kautukam — playfully; tena — by him (Baladeva); api — in turn; tat-nija-preshthaih — and by his own dear ones; dattam — was given; tat-preyasim — His beloved; prati — to.

5Sri Krishna gave it playfully as the gopis looked on; and Baladeva, with His own dear companions, passed it on to Krishna's beloved.

Verse 6

गोभिः समं प्रतिवनं प्रतिगच्छतोः श्री-
वक्त्रं मुकुन्दबलयोर्व्रजसुन्दरीभिः।
अक्षण्वतां फलमिदमिति गीतमत्र
शृण्वन् प्रभुः पुलकितः किल रोरवीति॥६॥

gobhiḥ samaṁ prativanaṁ pratigacchatoḥ śrī-
vaktraṁ mukundabalayorvrajasundarībhiḥ|
akṣaṇvatāṁ phalamidamiti gītamatra
śṛṇvan prabhuḥ pulakitaḥ kila roravīti||6||

gobhih — with the cows; samam — together; prativanam — from forest to forest; pratigacchatoh — going; shri-vaktram — the lovely face; mukunda-balayoh — of Mukunda and Bala; vraja-sundaribhih — by the beauties of Vraja; akshanvatam — of those who have eyes; phalam — the fruit; idam — this; iti — thus; gitam — sung; atra — here; shrinvan — hearing; prabhuh — the Lord; pulakitah — thrilling with joy; kila — indeed; roraviti — weeps aloud.

6'This is the fruit for those who have eyes…'2 — so the beauties of Vraja sang here of the lovely faces of Mukunda and Bala as they went with the cows from forest to forest." Hearing that song, the Lord, all thrilling, weeps aloud.

Verse 7

कुमुदाख्यवनं पश्य श्रीदामसुबलादिभिः।
सह संक्रीडतः कृष्णरामौ यत्र सुनिर्भरम्॥७॥

kumudākhyavanaṁ paśya śrīdāmasubalādibhiḥ|
saha saṁkrīḍataḥ kṛṣṇarāmau yatra sunirbharam||7||

kumuda-akhya-vanam — the forest named Kumuda; pashya — behold; shridama-subala-adibhih — with Shridama, Subala and the others; saha — together; samkridatah — sport; krishna-ramau — Krishna and Rama; yatra — where; su-nirbharam — to their hearts' content.

7"Behold the forest named Kumuda: here Krishna and Rama sport to Their hearts' content with Shridama, Subala and the others.

Verse 8

अत्र सरस्वतीतीरे अम्बिकाख्यं वनं जनैः।
पूज्यते शङ्करो देवो गौरी च व्रजवासिभिः॥८॥

atra sarasvatītīre ambikākhyaṁ vanaṁ janaiḥ|
pūjyate śaṅkaro devo gaurī ca vrajavāsibhiḥ||8||

atra — here; sarasvati-tire — on the bank of the Sarasvati; ambika-akhyam — named Ambika; vanam — (is) the forest; janaih — by the people; pujyate — is worshipped; shankarah — Shankara; devah — the god; gauri — Gauri; cha — and; vraja-vasibhih — by the residents of Vraja.

8Here, on the bank of the Sarasvati, is the forest called Ambika, where the people of Vraja worship the god Shankara and Gauri.

Verse 9

मुनेः शापात् सर्पदेहं प्राप्तो नाम सुदर्शनः।
नन्दार्धे गिलिते कृष्णेनोद्धृतः पादसंस्पृशन्॥९॥

muneḥ śāpāt sarpadehaṁ prāpto nāma sudarśanaḥ|
nandārdhe gilite kṛṣṇenoddhṛtaḥ pādasaṁspṛśan||9||

muneh — of a sage; shapat — through the curse; sarpa-deham — the body of a serpent; praptah — who had obtained; nama — named; sudarshanah — Sudarshana; nanda-ardhe — half of Nanda; gilite — having been swallowed; krishnena — by Krishna; uddhritah — was delivered; pada-samsprishan — by the touch of (His) foot.

9By a sage's curse a gandharva named Sudarshana had received the body of a serpent; when he had swallowed Nanda halfway, Krishna delivered him by the touch of His foot3.

Verse 10

गन्धर्व इति विख्यातस्तस्थौ सन्तोषयन् हरिम्।
ययावत्र निजं धाम कृष्णसंकीर्तनैर्मुदा॥१०॥

gandharva iti vikhyātastasthau santoṣayan harim|
yayāvatra nijaṁ dhāma kṛṣṇasaṁkīrtanairmudā||10||

gandharvah — a gandharva; iti — thus; vikhyatah — renowned; tasthau — stood; santoshayan — pleasing; harim — Hari; yayau — went; atra — from here; nijam — to his own; dhama — abode; krishna-samkirtanaih — with the glorification of Krishna; muda — joyfully.

10Renowned once more as a gandharva, he stood before Hari, pleasing Him with praise, and then from here he went joyfully to his own abode, glorifying Krishna.

Verse 11

वृषभानुपुरं पश्य यत्र वृन्दावनेश्वरी।
प्रादुर्भूता महालक्ष्मी राधा कृष्णविलासिनी॥११॥

vṛṣabhānupuraṁ paśya yatra vṛndāvaneśvarī|
prādurbhūtā mahālakṣmī rādhā kṛṣṇavilāsinī||11||

vrishabhanu-puram — the town of Vrishabhanu; pashya — behold; yatra — where; vrindavana-ishvari — the Queen of Vrindavana; pradurbhuta — appeared; maha-lakshmi — Mahalakshmi; radha — Radha; krishna-vilasini — who sports with Krishna.

11Behold the town of Vrishabhanu4 — here appeared Radha, the Queen of Vrindavana, Mahalakshmi, who sports with Krishna.

Verse 12

गिरिं रैवतकं पश्य बलदेवो रसाग्रणीः।
यत्र गोपीजनैः क्रीडन् द्विविदं परिचूर्णयत्॥१२॥

giriṁ raivatakaṁ paśya baladevo rasāgraṇīḥ|
yatra gopījanaiḥ krīḍan dvividaṁ paricūrṇayat||12||

girim — the hill; raivatakam — Raivataka; pashya — behold; baladevah — Baladeva; rasa-agranih — foremost in rasa; yatra — where; gopi-janaih — with the gopis; kridan — sporting; dvividam — Dvivida; parichurnayat — crushed to powder.

12Behold Raivataka Hill5 — here Baladeva, foremost in rasa, sporting with the gopis, crushed Dvivida to powder.

Verse 13

ययौ यामुनकं तीरं कालिन्दीं तां विकर्षयन्।
यथेच्छं जलमाविश्य क्रीडन् गोपीभिरच्युतः॥१३॥

yayau yāmunakaṁ tīraṁ kālindīṁ tāṁ vikarṣayan|
yathecchaṁ jalamāviśya krīḍan gopībhiracyutaḥ||13||

yayau — went; yamunakam — of the Yamuna; tiram — to the bank; kalindim — the Kalindi; tam — her; vikarshayan — dragging; yatha-iccham — at will; jalam — the water; avishya — entering; kridan — sporting; gopibhih — with the gopis; achyutah — the Unfallen.

13He went to the bank of the Yamuna, dragging the Kalindi6 to Himself, and, entering the water, the Unfallen One sported with the gopis to His heart's content.

Verse 14

तीरमासाद्य वासोभिर्विभूष्य भूषणैर्वरैः।
गोपीभिस्ता भूषयित्वा क्रीडति कृष्णकौतुकी॥१४॥

tīramāsādya vāsobhirvibhūṣya bhūṣaṇairvaraiḥ|
gopībhistā bhūṣayitvā krīḍati kṛṣṇakautukī||14||

tiram — the bank; asadya — reaching; vasobhih — with garments; vibhushya — adorning (himself); bhushanaih — with ornaments; varaih — fine; gopibhih — with the gopis; tah — them; bhushayitva — having adorned; kridati — sports; krishna-kautuki — whose delight is Krishna.

14Reaching the bank, He arrayed Himself in garments and fine ornaments, adorned His companions as well, and sports with the gopis — He whose delight is Krishna.

Verse 15

नन्दग्रामोत्तरे पश्य पावनाख्यं सरोवरम्।
यत्र नन्दस्य गोवत्साश्चरन्ति कृष्णपालिताः॥१५॥

nandagrāmottare paśya pāvanākhyaṁ sarovaram|
yatra nandasya govatsāścaranti kṛṣṇapālitāḥ||15||

nanda-grama-uttare — to the north of Nandagrama; pashya — behold; pavana-akhyam — named Pavana; saro-varam — the lake; yatra — where; nandasya — Nanda's; go-vatsah — cows and calves; charanti — graze; krishna-palitah — tended by Krishna.

15Behold, to the north of Nandagrama, the lake called Pavana, where Nanda's cows and calves graze, tended by Krishna.

Verse 16

नन्दीश्वरपश्चिमे च वनं हि काम्यपूर्वकम्।
पिच्छलाख्यः पर्वतोऽयमत्र तिष्ठति निर्मलः॥१६॥

nandīśvarapaścime ca vanaṁ hi kāmyapūrvakam|
picchalākhyaḥ parvato'yamatra tiṣṭhati nirmalaḥ||16||

nandishvara-pashchime — to the west of Nandishvara; cha — and; vanam — the forest; hi — indeed; kamya-purvakam — beginning with "Kamya" (Kamyavana); picchala-akhyah — named Picchala; parvatah — hill; ayam — this; atra — here; tishthati — stands; nirmalah — pure.

16And to the west of Nandishvara is the forest of Kamya7; here stands the pure hill called Picchala.

Verse 17

पिच्छले खेलतः कृष्णरामौ च बालकैः सह।
अरिष्टकेशिव्योमाद्या वृषाश्वमेषरूपिणः॥१७॥

picchale khelataḥ kṛṣṇarāmau ca bālakaiḥ saha|
ariṣṭakeśivyomādyā vṛṣāśvameṣarūpiṇaḥ||17||

picchale — on Picchala; khelatah — play; krishna-ramau — Krishna and Rama; cha — and; balakaih — with the boys; saha — together; arishta-keshi-vyoma-adyah — Arishta, Keshi, Vyoma and others; vrisha-ashva-mesha-rupinah — in the forms of a bull, a horse and a ram.

17On Picchala Krishna and Rama play with the boys. Arishta, Keshi, Vyoma and others — in the forms of a bull, a horse and a ram8 —

Verse 18

पञ्चत्वमापिताः कृष्णात् सर्वे मोक्षाधिकारिणः।
कृष्णोऽपि बालकैः सार्धं यत्र क्रीडति सर्वदा॥१८॥

pañcatvamāpitāḥ kṛṣṇāt sarve mokṣādhikāriṇaḥ|
kṛṣṇo'pi bālakaiḥ sārdhaṁ yatra krīḍati sarvadā||18||

panchatvam — to death; apitah — brought; krishnat — by Krishna; sarve — all; moksha-adhikarinah — made worthy of liberation; krishnah — Krishna; api — and; balakaih — with the boys; sardham — together; yatra — where; kridati — plays; sarvada — always.

18were all put to death by Krishna and became worthy of liberation. And here Krishna plays with the boys forever.

Verse 19

खदिराख्यं वनं रम्यं फलपुष्पसमन्वितम्।
मन्दवायुभिराकीर्णं पश्य गौराङ्गसुन्दर॥१९॥

khadirākhyaṁ vanaṁ ramyaṁ phalapuṣpasamanvitam|
mandavāyubhirākīrṇaṁ paśya gaurāṅgasundara||19||

khadira-akhyam — named Khadira; vanam — the forest; ramyam — lovely; phala-pushpa-samanvitam — full of fruits and flowers; manda-vayubhih — with gentle breezes; akirnam — pervaded; pashya — behold; gauranga-sundara — O beautiful Gauranga.

19Behold, beautiful Gauranga, the forest named Khadira — lovely, full of fruits and flowers, pervaded by gentle breezes.

Verse 20

अत्रैव गोपीभिः सार्धं राधाकृष्णौ निरन्तरम्।
क्रीडतः कौतुकाविष्टौ क्रयविक्रयलीलया॥२०॥

atraiva gopībhiḥ sārdhaṁ rādhākṛṣṇau nirantaram|
krīḍataḥ kautukāviṣṭau krayavikrayalīlayā||20||

atra — here; eva — indeed; gopibhih — with the gopis; sardham — together; radha-krishnau — Radha and Krishna; nirantaram — ceaselessly; kridatah — play; kautuka-avishtau — filled with merriment; kraya-vikraya-lilaya — with the game of buying and selling.

20Here Radha and Krishna, with the gopis, full of merriment, ceaselessly play at buying and selling9.

Verse 21

निकुञ्जनवमल्लिकानवतमालसालार्जुनै-
रशोकनवमाधवीनवरसालसङ्घैः किल।
मयूरशुककोकिलै रभसमेव संशोभिते
सुपुष्पपरिसंस्थितौ जयत एव राधामाधवौ॥२१॥

nikuñjanavamallikānavatamālasālārjunai-
raśokanavamādhavīnavarasālasaṅghaiḥ kila|
mayūraśukakokilai rabhasameva saṁśobhite
supuṣpaparisaṁsthitau jayata eva rādhāmādhavau||21||

nikunja-nava-mallika-nava-tamala-sala-arjunaih — with bowers, fresh jasmine, young tamalas, salas and arjunas; ashoka-nava-madhavi-nava-rasala-sanghaih — with ashokas, fresh madhavi creepers and clusters of young mango trees; kila — truly; mayura-shuka-kokilaih — with peacocks, parrots and cuckoos; rabhasam — ardently; eva — indeed; samshobhite — in (the place) adorned; su-pushpa-parisamsthitau — abiding amid lovely flowers; jayatah — triumph; eva — indeed; radha-madhavau — Radha and Madhava.

21Amid the bowers, the fresh jasmine, the young tamalas, salas and arjunas, amid the ashokas, the fresh madhavi creepers and the clusters of young mango trees, in a place ardently adorned by peacocks, parrots and cuckoos, abiding among lovely flowers — Radha and Madhava triumph!

Verse 22

सुरम्यसखीचातुरीचरितचारुवंशीस्वनैः
प्रगल्भतरुणीजनैर्हसितगीतनृत्योत्सवैः।
सहैव सततं स्मरमदनयुक्तलीलापरौ
रासेश्वरी-रासेश्वरौ रसविशेषपालोत्सुकौ॥२२॥

suramyasakhīcāturīcaritacāruvaṁśīsvanaiḥ
pragalbhataruṇījanairhasitagītanṛtyotsavaiḥ|
sahaiva satataṁ smaramadanayuktalīlāparau
rāseśvarī-rāseśvarau rasaviśeṣapālotsukau||22||

su-ramya-sakhi-chaturi-charita-charu-vamshi-svanaih — with the sweet sounds of the flute and the clever doings of charming friends; pragalbha-taruni-janaih — with bold young maidens; hasita-gita-nritya-utsavaih — with festivals of laughter, song and dance; saha — together; eva — indeed; satatam — ever; smara-madana-yukta-lila-parau — devoted to pastimes full of the intoxication of Smara; rasa-ishvari-rasa-ishvarau — the Queen and the King of the rasa dance; rasa-vishesha-pala-utsukau — eager to cherish a special rasa.

22Ever together — with the sweet sounds of the flute and the clever doings of their charming friends, with bold young maidens, with festivals of laughter, song and dance — devoted to pastimes full of the intoxication of Kama10, the Queen and the King of the rasa dance are eager to cherish a special rasa."

Verse 23

राधाकृष्णविलासवैभवरसं श्रुत्वा रुदन्नप्यसौ
तत्तद्रूपप्रकटनपरो माधुरीधुर्यसारम्।
व्यक्तीकृत्य स जगति पुनर्गोष्ठभावेन पूर्णः
सान्द्रानन्दो विजयति परं श्रीशचीनन्दनोऽयम्॥२३॥

rādhākṛṣṇavilāsavaibhavarasaṁ śrutvā rudannapyasau
tattadrūpaprakaṭanaparo mādhurīdhuryasāram|
vyaktīkṛtya sa jagati punargoṣṭhabhāvena pūrṇaḥ
sāndrānando vijayati paraṁ śrīśacīnandano'yam||23||

radha-krishna-vilasa-vaibhava-rasam — the rasa of the splendour of Radha and Krishna's pastimes; shrutva — having heard; rudan — weeping; api — though; asau — He; tat-tad-rupa-prakatana-parah — intent on manifesting each of those forms; madhuri-dhurya-saram — the essence of the pre-eminence of sweetness; vyaktikritya — having revealed; sah — He; jagati — in the world; punah — again; goshtha-bhavena — with the mood of the cowherd village; purnah — filled; sandra-anandah — dense bliss; vijayati — triumphs; param — supremely; shri-shachi-nandanah — Sri Shachinandana; ayam — this.

23Hearing of the splendour of Radha and Krishna's pastimes, He, though weeping, was intent on manifesting each of those forms; and, having again revealed to the world the essence of supreme sweetness, filled with the mood of the cowherd village, dense bliss itself — this Sri Shachinandana triumphs above all!

Thus ends the tenth sarga, "Beholding the Sacred Bowers, the Yamuna and Other Places" (Shri-nikunja-yamuna-adi-darshana), of the fourth prakrama of the poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita."

✦

Notes

  1. Bhagavata Purana 10.34.25–32. The name Syamantaka, which there belongs to another jewel (10.56), is here given to Shankhachuda's gem.
  2. The opening of the gopis' song in the Bhagavata Purana (10.21.7): "This is the fruit for those who have eyes; we know no other…"
  3. Bhagavata Purana 10.34.1–18: in the Ambika forest, where the cowherds had come for a festival of Shiva, a serpent seized Nanda; at the touch of Krishna's foot he became the gandharva Sudarshana again.
  4. Vrishabhanu is Radha's father; his town is Barsana.
  5. In the Bhagavata Purana (10.67) Baladeva slays the ape Dvivida on Raivataka Hill near Dvaraka; here the place is shown in Vraja.
  6. The Kalindi is the Yamuna. Baladeva, intoxicated with varuni, called the Yamuna to Him, and when she did not come He dragged her with His plough (Bhagavata Purana 10.65.24–32); there too, on leaving the water, He receives garments and ornaments.
  7. Kamyavana: one of the twelve forests of Vraja.
  8. Arishta in the form of a bull, Keshi in the form of a horse (Bhagavata Purana 10.36–37); Vyoma carried off the boys who were playing "sheep and thieves" (ibid. 10.37.26–33).
  9. Probably the game in which the gopis sell Krishna milk and butter and He haggles with them.
  10. Kama (in the text, Smara and Madana): the god of love. The "kama" of Radha and Krishna's pastimes is not worldly passion seeking its own pleasure but pure prema, which seeks only Krishna's joy; it merely bears the name of Kama (cf. Bhakti-rasamrita-sindhu 1.2.285: "the prema of the cowherd women became renowned by the name 'kama'").
